description: SYNTHETIC calibration class for the near-duplicate thresholds (SENTINELEDU_TASKS.md 7.3). Typed answers, 10 students, questions from data/rubrics/sample_rubric.json. Not a substitute for planted pairs in the real gold set (task 1.6).

s01.Q1: In my words photosynthesis is like a kitchen inside the leaf where sunshine is the stove and the plant cooks sugar out of air and water.
s01.Q3: Water is needed for photosynthesis to make glucose, and it carries minerals up from the roots to the leaves of the plant.

s02.Q1: Photosynthesis is basically a kitchen in the leaf, the sunshine works as the stove and the plant cooks sugar from the air and water.
s02.Q3: Plants use water as a raw material in photosynthesis and it also keeps their cells turgid so the plant stands up straight.

s03.Q1: Photosynthesis is the process in which green plants use energy from sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose and release oxygen.
s03.Q3: Plants drink water mostly so their stems do not flop over like a wet noodle, and I think the water also travels up like a lift carrying food salts to every leaf.

s04.Q1: Green plants make their own food by photosynthesis. Chlorophyll traps light and the plant combines carbon dioxide with water to form glucose, giving out oxygen.
s04.Q3: Plants take in water mainly so the stem does not flop over like a soggy noodle, and the water also goes up like an elevator carrying food salts to all the leaves.

s05.Q1: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants make their own food. Using the energy of sunlight, the plant combines carbon dioxide and water to produce glucose.
s05.Q3: Water is one of the raw materials of photosynthesis, so a plant cannot make food without it. Water also carries dissolved mineral salts such as nitrates from the soil up to the leaves.

s06.Q1: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants make their own food. Using the energy of sunlight the plant combines carbon dioxide and water to produce glucose, a simple sugar.
s06.Q3: Water is one of the raw materials of photosynthesis so a plant cannot make food without it. Water also carries dissolved mineral salts such as nitrate from the soil up to the leaves.

s07.Q1: It is when leaves catch light with their green stuff and use that power to glue carbon dioxide and water together into sugar, and oxygen escapes.
s07.Q3: Without water a plant wilts because its cells lose their firmness, and it also cannot make food because water is used in photosynthesis.

s08.Q1: It is when leafs catch light with there green stuff and use that power to glue carbon dioxide and water together into sugar and oxygen escapes.
s08.Q3: Water cools the plant when it evaporates from the leaves and it is used to make sugar during photosynthesis in the chloroplasts.

s09.Q1: Plants produce glucose in their leaves during photosynthesis, using light energy, water from the roots and carbon dioxide from the air.
s09.Q3: When I forget my plant at home on Sundays it droops, so water must be what holds up the leaves, and it brings nutrients from the soil too.

s10.Q1: During photosynthesis a plant uses sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make food in the form of sugar, and oxygen is released into the air.
s10.Q3: My plant at home droops on Sundays when I forget it, so water must be what holds the leaves up, and it also brings nutrients from soil.
